He said: I thought he was only reciting it to make known the sanctity of the city.

﴿And this secure city﴾, meaning Makkah, the safe place. Al-Farra' recited a verse of poetry:

*Do you not know, O Asma', woe to you, that I*
*have sworn an oath that I will not betray my trustee (amini)?*

He intends "amini," meaning "secure."

﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, meaning the most balanced form and the finest appearance. This is because He created every other thing bent over on its face, except man. Abu Bakr ibn Zahir said: [He is] adorned with intellect, disciplined by command, refined by discernment, tall of stature, taking his food in his hand.

﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, meaning to the most decrepit age, when his lifespan diminishes, his body weakens and his intellect departs.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Some men were returned to the most decrepit age in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed their excuse, and informed that for them is the reward of what they did before their intellects departed.

'Ikrimah said: The great age of this aged elder does not harm him, if Allah, exalted is He, concludes his life with the best of what he used to do.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: "The lowest" means the weak, the aged and the chronically ill. His saying ﴿lowest of the low﴾ is indefinite, encompassing the whole category, as you say: "So-and-so is the most generous standing man." When you make it definite, you say: "the standing men."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mihran told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Farra'i told us, saying: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id told us, saying: Khalid al-Zayyat told us, saying: Dawud Abu Sulayman told us, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ma'mar ibn Hazm al-Ansari, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For a newborn until he reaches puberty (al-hinth), whatever good deed he does is recorded for his parents; if he does a bad deed, it is not recorded against him or against his parents. When he reaches puberty and the pen runs over him, Allah commands the two angels with him to protect him and guide him. When he reaches forty years in Islam, Allah, glorified is He, grants him security from the three afflictions: madness, leprosy and vitiligo. When he reaches fifty, Allah lightens his reckoning. When he reaches sixty, Allah grants him the inclination to turn to Him in what He loves. When he reaches seventy, the inhabitants of the heavens love him. When he reaches eighty, Allah records his good deeds and overlooks his bad deeds. When he reaches ninety, Allah forgives him what he has done previously and what he will do later, grants him intercession for the people of his household, and his name becomes 'Prisoner of Allah on earth.' When he reaches the lowest age, ﴿so that he knows nothing after knowing﴾, Allah, glorified is He, records for him the like of what he used to do of good in his health. And if he does a bad deed, it is not recorded against him." [182] [[Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 3/217. Kanz al-'Ummal: 15/766, no. 43011.]]

al-Hasan, Mujahid and Qatadah said: "Then We return him" means: to the Fire. Abu al-'Aliyah said: It means: to the Fire, in the worst form, in the form of a pig.

Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Hawwas told us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Hubayrah, on the authority of 'Ali, who said:

The gates of Hell are some below others. It begins with the lowest and fills it. So it is the lowest of the low.

In the codex of 'Abd Allah, it is "asfala as-safilina" with an alif (as a plural in the accusative, reading "lowest of the low" with a different form). Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, so their intellects have departed and their deeds have been cut off, and no good deed is established for them, ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ from among them. For it is recorded for them, in their state of decrepitude and senility, the like of what they used to do in their state of youth, health and strength. That is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿For them is a reward never cut off﴾. Al-Dahhak said: a reward without deed. Then He said, establishing the proof and rebuking the disbelievers:

﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgement, O man, after this?﴾ — after this proof and demonstration — ﴿the Recompense?﴾, meaning the reckoning and the requital.

﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾

Qatadah said: We have been told that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when he recited this verse, would say: "Yes, and I am among the witnesses to that." [183]
